en: Surely you two have something to do yourselves?
Yah. How 'bout I go instead of you? Can't have my own mentor doin' my work for me.
'Sides, Okudera-han, ya can't be over yer injuries already. Ya still need rest.
Hmph. Well, do as you will.
Reduces health loss from being in the cold.
Huh, didn't know anybody owned trucks here.
None of the villagers do. The guy with the truck is a trader who visits us to conduct business. He must be stuck here because of the road closure.
We sell him animal skins and meat, and he sells us goods from the city. Even in this place, commerce is everything.
Yeah, just like everywhere else. Guess I'll be doin' business with him myself soon.
So go introduce yourself. If you're going to be working with somebody, it's always best to know each other's names.
You made it back safely. The mountain was kind to you.
Tell me when you decide to go hunting again. Until then, I'll hold on to your rifle. Okay?
Sure, nice of ya.
If you collect an item on the mountain and want to use it elsewhere, move it to your Inventory when you return to the village.

Upon return, items you collected on the mountain are moved to the Item Box.
Transfer the ones you want to use to your Inventory. The deer meat for
Nishina's wife has been automatically moved to Valuables.
Raises walking speed in the snow.
What're ya doin' with that shovel?
Huh? Oh, I was going to dig up some meat I buried here last fall.
Ya buried some meat?
Yes, the ground acts as a natural freezer, so the meat can stay there all winter without spoiling. We store food this way for emergencies.
Alright. Uh, so if yer diggin' it up... does that mean there's an emergency?
...I suppose you could call it that.
(So she shared food with me when they were already running low...)
Is yer husband out huntin'? Saw some deer on the mountain yesterday.
No, because Okudera-san left on a hunt this morning. While he's out there, none of the others will go.
They say that Yama-oroshi is more likely to attack when Okudera-san's scent is in the air. Just like that day nine years ago.
So, yer husband stays at home, afraid to hunt, and then makes ya come out here an' dig up meat?
Huh? Oh, no, no... It's not like that. I just thought today was a good day to do this.
Oh! Here it is!
This meat from last fall has more fat on it than the meat hunted at other times of the year.
Interestin'.
Here... for you.
Eh? Why for me?
You're going after Okudera-san again, aren't you?
Sure, might be, but...
Well, better safe than sorry.
But... ain't ya in need of this food?
Yes. But I can't turn my back on someone determined to go to the mountain in this blizzard.
If it makes you feel any better about it, come back and share food with me if you happen to gather any while you're on the mountain.
I will. That's a promise.
In the past, we all used to help each other out like this.
That's the kind of village I remember, at least. Please, be careful out there.
You're Saejima-san, aren't you?
How'd ya know my name?
Okudera-san told me to look out for a big man almost two meters tall, and if he tried to leave the village, I should stop him.
Okudera-san doesn't want a repeat of the tragedy nine years ago.
What tragedy?
Yama-oroshi attacked our village.
Yama-oroshi. Ya mean that giant bear?
Yeah. At the time, Okudera lived with his hunting partner, a man named Sato. He was a good guy. But one day...
Sato was pursuing Yama-oroshi, and ended up chasing him straight into the village. It was terrifying for all of us.
You see, that day, Sato heard that Yama-oroshi had been spotted, so he took it upon himself to go eliminate the menace.
There was a blizzard that day, too.
And? What happened?
Sato went missing. Okudera-san went after him, and was injured badly. And that's... when it happened.
Yama-oroshi's attack on the village?
Yes. Thankfully, nobody died. That was a miracle in and of itself.
But buildings were knocked flat, and every last morsel of food in storage was eaten.
Getting through the winter is always tough. Losing our entire food supplies like that... it was devastating. You can't imagine.
We were pushed to the very brink of starvation.
That's terrible.
Ever since then, Okudera-san's been shunned by the rest of the village.
And every winter, when it's snowing hard, he still takes to the mountain in search of Yama-oroshi.
He shows no consideration for the other hunters.
Maybe he's trying to get revenge for what Yama-oroshi did nine years ago. That's what the rest of us think, anyway.
An' that's what he's doin' right now?
No, he said he had an errand today. Something about finding Yama-oroshi's food source.
(He means Baba-chan.)
(Tellin' Okudera-han about Yama-oroshi has stirred up trouble...)
Look, you don't need to know any of this, anyway. You shouldn't go up to the mountain⑬you'll just be another guy to worry about.
Trust me, you should just go home.
Hey, hold on there.
You're the one who got hauled into the village this morning, right? I've got something to ask you.
I'm Nishina. I'm what you might call the leader of the hunters.
So there's a huntin' community here.
Yeah. It's a dying way of life, but we're still here for now.
Traditional hunters have called this village home ever since it was founded.
What was it ya wanted to ask me?
We're worried... about another guy who's also a visitor to our town, much like yourself. We don't know what he's going to do next.
What other visitor?
Okudera. The man who brought you in.
He's a newcomer?
No, not a newcomer. He's lived in the village a long time, actually. But he's still considered a visitor, because he's not originally from here.
In fact, I don't know where he came from. One of our hunters found him in the woods one day. He was lost, so the hunter brought him back to the village. Then he just... stayed.
That was ten years ago. Ever since, he's only been trouble to us locals.
(Looks like there ain't no love lost 'tween the villagers and Okudera-han.)
So, what's concernin' ya?
I heard he went to the mountain this morning. Is it because the monster was sighted?
Monster?
Yama-oroshi. He's a giant, man-eating bear. Twice the size of a regular bear.
Yeah? Huh. Sounds like the bear that attacked me.
What!? You were attacked by Yama-oroshi?
I mean, I ain't sure or nothin', but it fits yer description of the beast.
Does Okudera know about this?
Yeah, 'course.
Then... that's why... Agh, there's no time to explain! I have to tell the others.
Yes! If you don't plan on dying today, go inside and lock up tight!
Whatever you do, don't go chasing after Okudera. You understand!?
(Musta been some trouble here... Somethin' to do with Okudera-han and that man-eatin' bear.)
(Who woulda thought there'd be a village this deep in the mountains...)
(Damn, and it's mornin' already. How long was I out?)
Rgh! This cold is brutal. Even my bones feel frozen! Gotta hurry before I lose too much strength...
On the mountain, the cold drains your health over time. Restore it by eating food!
If your health gets too low, open the Pause Menu and consume an item that restores it.
Gotta stick to the river for now.
Gotta meet up with Okudera-han.
Bear tracks. Pretty close to the village...
Blood! Was there a bear attack?
A blood trail. Better follow it.
Already pretty high in altitude. Where are ya, Baba?
Saejima! What are you doing here?
Came to tell ya that Baba-chan woke up.
Also... I can't stand bein' a burden on ya anymore. I wanna try huntin' my own food, at least.
And I gotta repay the person who shared her food with me, even when she don't have much for herself.
That getup. That gun. Where'd you get them? Please don't tell me you stole them.
No, it's all legit. I pled my case to some kindly folks, and they let me borrow this stuff. Lotta kind people in the village, actually... Why don't ya try befriendin' them some time?
Hmph. It's none of your business.
Okay, that's fine, Okudera-han. But I still wanna hunt. Can ya teach me the basics?
Fine, I'll do it. My life will be easier when you're not just another mouth to feed, anyway.
Okay, the basics.
Okay, listen close if you're serious about learning to hunt and trap.
Today, I'll teach you how to use your rifle.
To shoot game?
Yes. Now usually, after a shooting session, a gun needs to be properly cleaned and serviced. But that's an involved process... one I don't feel like teaching you, frankly.
So I'll just clean it myself whenever you come back from the mountain. That way, you only have to carry it when you're hunting. Less tedium for both of us.
Sure. Less tedium, and less work for me.
Exactly. Now, obviously, you can't shoot accurately if you're too far away.
If you spot game, you have to approach it without letting it see you. The key is to make yourself small and quiet.
You just crouch down and creep forward. Try it.

Press <Action:Button_Circle@Hunter_And_Killer> to crouch. By moving in this position, your
prey is less likely to notice you, and you'll have greater
greater accuracy while shooting.
This used to be a hunting hut. I haven't been to this one in a while⑬I typically use the other ones...
But what a shame to see it like this. Bears must have knocked it flat.
This is Yama-oroshi's doin'?

Who knows? Other bears may not be as strong or big as he is, but they could still do something like this. Such a shame... But at least it can be fixed with a <Color:8>hut repair kit<Color:Default> from the village.
If you fix it, it could be used as a hunting hut again.
There are a number of flattened huts on the mountain.
If fixed with a <Color:8>hut repair kit<Color:Default>, a hunting hut will be usable as a checkpoint. If you fail a mission, you can restart the mission at the hut you last visited.
Rest at a hunting hut to restock your ammunition. And just like a hideout, the hut restores your health over time.

If you become too weak to continue, you can make an emergency return to the village from any hunting hut. However, if you do this, you will lose all items obtained during the outing, as well as any mission progress.
Sure, but it ain't like I got the money for buyin' any hut repair kit. That'll have to wait.
That's the way of a hunter's life... He's poor until he catches his prey. Why don't we try to rectify that now? Let's look for some deer.
Ya don't have to convince me.

You can (and should) sell items you acquire on the
mountain. Your only source of income in the village
is what you manage to hunt, trap, and harvest.
Okudera-han, whaddya make of these tracks?
Definitely deer tracks, and they're fresh. The deer are probably close by.

You may find animal tracks on the mountain.
Follow them to locate prey.
So, follow 'em?
Yes, and from here on out, keep the chatter to a minimum. Let's use hand signals.

Press <Action:Button_L2@Hunter_And_Killer> to signal your (NPC) companion. There
are two commands: "Come with me" and "Stay put."
Okay, listen. If you spot some deer, approach them from behind carefully.
Get as close as possible, then shoot. Got that?
Today I'll show you how to trap small game. It doesn't involve any shooting, so don't worry about your rifle.
You have to use different traps for different animals. Today we'll catch rabbits. For them, we use snares.
Got it. Rabbits, snares.
Yeah. You can also catch martens and foxes around here, but we'll save them for another time.
So, this is a snare.
When the animal steps in it, the wire tightens around its foot.
You can use mine today, but remember to bring your own for next time.
You got a <Color:8>Snare<Color:Default>.
Traps are reusable, but they can break. Just repair them if that happens.
Each time you use a trap, it gets a little less durable. If its durability drops to zero, it will break. Use a <Color:8>repair kit<Color:Default> to repair it.
The key to successful trapping is placement.
You have to look for a good trap site.
Where do I find those?
There are many <Color:7>trap sites<Color:Default> on the mountain, but the best ones are wherever there are lots of animal tracks. So if you find a site, check the area for tracks!
So... I gotta trek around in the snow until I find a site?
Nobody ever said a hunter's life was easy. Go on, now. Lead the way.
Alright.
Return to the village?
Whenever you're out here, always be wary of bears. Yama-oroshi is the obvious danger, but other bears are nothing to be trifled with, either.
